title: Explicit resolved cohomology presheaf and sheafification comparison
statement: Let C be a site and R a commutative sheaf of rings, with the universe and sheafification hypotheses of [def-per-local-rhom-normalization-interface]. For a complex L and integer n, the functor taking a complex X to degree n cohomology of the presheaf complex underlying Hom(L,I(X)), for the fixed functorial K-injective resolution I, inverts quasi-isomorphisms. Its localization P_L^n has a natural sheafification isomorphism to degree n cohomology of internal derived Hom from QL. Transporting the source by any isomorphism QL to K gives the corresponding comparison for K. For a K-injective target, the representative comparison is normalized by the fixed augmentation.

proof.text: Take the fixed functorial K-injective resolution I. Naturality of its augmentation and two-out-of-three show that I maps quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. The section Hom quasi-isomorphism theorem shows that every section of the underlying Hom presheaf map induces an isomorphism on cohomology. Evaluation computes module-presheaf cohomology, so the Hom presheaf cohomology functor inverts quasi-isomorphisms and has a localization P. Exact sheafification commutes with complex homology; the sheafification counit on an underlying sheaf is invertible. Combine those comparisons with the fixed product-localization factorization defining internal derived Hom. Full faithfulness of precomposition with Q descends their natural isomorphism to P followed by sheafification. Transport source isomorphisms by contravariance. For a K-injective target, Hom applied to its augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism; invert its localization and compose with the fixed coefficient factorization. Cancelling the inverse proves its normalization.

proof_origin.place: The local Hom comparison and its normalizations, Tags 0A8Y, 0A94 and 0A95
